quote: I'm not sure that I'm not sure that I'm not sure that I'm not sure
stewart_read: Rep's intro devolves into a repeated stall phrase, failing to establish clean legitimacy in the critical first 30 seconds.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a transcription artifact rather than actual rep speech, but even so the effect on the call (confusion) is real.
coaching_implication: Rehearse a clean, single-pass intro line so a technical hiccup doesn't compound into repeated garbled loops.

quote: I just I was wondering how much it would cost and what's the rebates on it and all that
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a direct interest reason (cost/rebates) but the rep never circles back to frame the appointment around answering that specific curiosity.
coaching_implication: Rep should tie the eventual bill/design conversation explicitly back to 'this is exactly how we'll show you the cost and rebates' to use the stated reason as a hook.

quote: Are you on the title of the home as well? No. That's my daughter.
stewart_read: The actual homeowner (Amy) is not on the call at all — Ira is a proxy for his daughter — yet the call proceeds through qualifiers as if this were a normal path to booking.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep should have flagged early that any appointment must include Amy directly, similar to spouse/adult-child inclusion protocol.
coaching_implication: When the actual decision-maker is absent from the call, rep should explicitly confirm Amy will be the one on any scheduled appointment before going deep into her qualifiers.

stewart_read: Nearly two minutes of dead air pass while the customer searches for a bill before the rep intervenes; this matches the schema's flagged failure to pivot within 2 minutes.
coaching_implication: Rep should have proactively offered the photo/online-account alternative at the first sign of a fruitless paper search, not after multiple minutes of silence.

quote: we're looking for a copy of her twelve months of COVID in person.
stewart_read: Second touch of the same bill-search friction pattern — rep re-asks for the document without an efficient alternative path offered yet.
coaching_implication: Same coaching point as the first touch — introduce the photo/text alternative immediately rather than after silent searching.

quote: I can just send you a request and then if you have a call back later then you can do it that way as well.
stewart_read: Third touch — rep finally pivots to the deferred/photo path, the correct move but delayed by minutes of unproductive search.
coaching_implication: Credit the eventual pivot but coach on speed — this should have happened at the first search failure, not the third.

quote: K. Yeah. Probably $300 a month or so.
stewart_read: Bill amount captured but never flipped into an emotional lever against the utility — rep just restates the number and moves to the account/bill-document ask.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect the $300/month figure back as the villain (e.g., tie it to the high-efficiency AC/heat comment the customer volunteered) to build urgency before pivoting to the bill document ask.
